title: Dense prime random distribution correctness
objective: Replace low-bit-biased packed GF(p) matrix random generation with deterministic statistically sane uniform residues, preserving public semantics and performance

oracles: Independent deterministic reference sampler and structural GF(2) rank tests

handoff.summary: Dense packed GF(p) random construction now partitions the accepted 32-bit LCG state interval into p equal high-order buckets instead of reducing the generator's weak low bits modulo p. Rejection and state transitions are unchanged, so seeded calls and the shared stream remain reproducible. Direct native and dynamic-fallback tests verify exact reference output, range, state, GF(2) balance, non-alternation, and public ranks near full size. Previously degenerate 79/80/81 binary matrices now have ranks 79/79/81; the formerly all-zero MatrixSpace(GF(2),80) sample has rank 79. Warm 500x500 construction medians remain 1.03-1.86 ms across GF(2), GF(97), random_matrix, and MatrixSpace.random_element.
risks: The shared 32-bit LCG is deterministic and now mapped exactly uniformly over each accepted word interval, but it is not a cryptographic or high-dimensional statistical generator.
The generic scalar _random_int helper still maps accepted multiword values by remainder; auditing that broader random API and its integer bulk-kernel parity is separate work.
next_steps: Integrate the compiler dependency commit followed by this RNG commit and rebuild the production dense-prime artifact.
Consider a separate repository-wide random-stream audit before promising a stable long-term seeded sequence.
